title: The ordered character product as an internal inhomogeneous bar cocycle
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring and $G$ any profinite group, in the sizes and internal module categories of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $H$ be internal functions and $B$ its inhomogeneous bar diagram of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data], with the trivial regular coefficient. For every ordered list $a=(a_1,\dots,a_q)$ of additive condensed characters of [def-sfb-condensed-unipotent-class], there exists a cochain map $c:A[-q]\to U^\bullet$, whose transported degree-q component (as in [def-sfb-internal-bar-character-data]) has on every profinite $S$, scalar $r\in A(S)$, base change $f:T\to S$ and tuple $g_i\in C(T,G)$ the internal-function value $f^*r\prod_{i=1}^q a_i(g_i)$. For the empty list the product is 1. This statement is independent of a homogeneous resolution or deletion maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-written internal-bar expansion, extracted from lem-sfb-internal-bar-character-lifts.

proof.text: For r on S, define a family on every T over S by f* r times the product of character values. The naturality of every character and of ring multiplication proves restriction compatibility. Use the evaluation equivalence of the internal functions to obtain a section. Its addition, scalar and restriction equations give an internal linear map from the regular module into the degree-q internal functions.

Transport through B.term and evaluate the differential using B.face. The trivial action makes the first face drop g_1. Use partial products T_j=product_{k<j} a_k(g_k) product_{k>=j} a_k(g_(k+1)), with 0-based character indices k and tuple entries g_0,...,g_q. The first dropping face is T_0, and the final dropping face is T_q. Interior face i (1<=i<=q) has value T_i+T_(i-1), by expanding a_(i-1)(g_(i-1) g_i) with additivity. Its signed sum is T_0 + sum_{i=1}^q (-1)^i(T_i+T_(i-1)) + (-1)^(q+1)T_q = 0, since each T_j occurs with opposite signs. In degree zero this is 1-1. All identities remain true after multiplying by the restricted scalar.

Evaluation is injective, so the differential of the internal map is zero. Use mkHomFromSingle and extension along embeddingUpNat to obtain the cochain map. Cancel the single and term isomorphisms to recover the displayed scalar formula.

theorem exists_product_cocycle
    {H : CategoryTheory.CondensedBar.InternalFunctions A}
    (B : CategoryTheory.CondensedBar.BarDiagram (G := G) H)
    (a : List (Character A G)) :
    ∃ c : (HomologicalComplex.single (Modules A.toMon) (.up ℤ) (a.length : ℤ)).obj
        (Mod.regular A.X) ⟶ CategoryTheory.CondensedBar.extend
          ((CategoryTheory.CondensedBar.cochains B).obj
            ((trivial (R := A.toMon) (P := G)).obj (Mod.regular A.X))),
    ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (r : CategoryTheory.CondensedBar.sectionRing A S)
      (T : Profinite.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (g : Fin a.length → C(T, G)),
    (H.evaluate (CategoryTheory.CondensedBar.power G a.length) S (Mod.regular A.X)
      (onSections A.toMon (cocycleComponent B c) S r)).val T f
        (CategoryTheory.CondensedBar.tupleMap g) =
      (InternalAbelianSheafModule.sectionRingSheaf
        (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) A.X).obj.map f.op r *
          ∏ k : Fin a.length, (a.get k).app T (g k)
